title: ZOCOR (simvastatin) tablets, for oral use: full prescribing information
authors: US Food and Drug Administration (labelling submitted by Organon LLC)
journal: US Food and Drug Administration approved prescribing information, via DailyMed; version 11, effective 28 March 2025; sections 4 to 8
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement
result: Contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, ciclosporin, danazol and gemfibrozil, in acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis, and in hypersensitivity, with anaphylaxis, angioedema and Stevens-Johnson syndrome reported. In a study of 12,064 survivors of myocardial infarction (mean 6.7 years), myopathy (creatine kinase above 10 times the upper limit of normal) occurred in about 0.02% on 20 mg and 0.9% on 80 mg, and rhabdomyolysis (creatine kinase above 40 times) in about 0% and 0.4%, highest in the first year. In a study of 10,269 patients on 40 mg (mean 5 years), myopathy or rhabdomyolysis below 0.1%. In patients at high cardiovascular risk on 40 mg (median 3.9 years), myopathy in about 0.05% of 7367 non-Chinese and 0.24% of 5468 Chinese patients, and 1.24% in Chinese patients given extended-release niacin 2 g/day in addition. Acute kidney injury secondary to myoglobinuria and rare fatalities have occurred. Rare immune-mediated necrotising myopathy. Persistent transaminases above 3 times the upper limit of normal in about 1% of patients in clinical studies; rare postmarketing fatal and non-fatal hepatic failure. In 4S (median 5.4 years) diabetes mellitus was reported in 4.2% on simvastatin against 3.6% on placebo. Postmarketing reports: anaemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, haemolytic anaemia; pancreatitis; hepatitis, jaundice, fatal and non-fatal hepatic failure; hypersensitivity syndrome including anaphylaxis, angioedema, lupus erythematosus-like syndrome, dermatomyositis and vasculitis; immune-mediated necrotising myopathy, polymyalgia rheumatica; depression, paraesthesia, peripheral neuropathy; cognitive impairment, generally non-serious and reversible, onset 1 day to years, median resolution 3 weeks; new-onset or exacerbated myasthenia gravis; toxic epidermal necrolysis, erythema multiforme including Stevens-Johnson syndrome; interstitial lung disease; erectile dysfunction. Pregnancy: may cause fetal harm based on the mechanism of action; breastfeeding not recommended.
